newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer amid strength in dlr.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer amid strength in dlr.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened mostly firmer in quiet trade on Monday, boosted by strength in the Canadian dollar and expectations U.S. interest rates will remain steady this week, analysts said.
"It's a fairly steady market. Probably a bit of influence is the buoyancy of the Canadian dollar," said Barry Davenport, senior vice-president of treasury with Bank of Montreal.
"We're opening up at the beginning of the week on a fairly positive tone."
Canada's three-month cash T-bill firmed to yield 2.85 percent from 2.86 percent at Friday's close.
Canada's dollar opened stronger at C$1.3444 (US$0.7438) from Friday's close of C$1.3470 (US$0.7423) on the back of broad-based buying from U.K. funds and U.S. accounts during European trading.

Strength in Canadian financial markets stems partly from U.S. economic data out last week showing inflation there remains subdued, said Davenport. He said the tame data has increased expectations that U.S. interest rates will be held steady at this week's meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee.
Dealers said while flows were light in the Canadian T-bill market buying interest was widespread.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.19 percent from 3.21 percent.
The one-year when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.58 percent from 3.60 percent at Friday's close.
The call loan rate or overnight lending rate traded at 3.05 percent, near the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
